name: harness-captured-token-reaches-the-coordinator
description: R15, CARRY HALF. A fixture can express a value the coordinator MINTS at run time. The second preflight opens a snapshot session; the server mints `session_token` and the fixture captures it under the name `minted_session_token`. The main request substitutes those exact bytes into its own body, and the coordinator answers as it would for that session -- ok:true with the pinned version from the cut. The proof this fixture is not decorative is the control in test_effect_fence_corpus.py: the SAME request with a well-formed but never-minted token answers ok:false / session_invalidated, so the affirmative answer here is caused by the captured bytes and by nothing else. Before this unit the harness discarded every preflight response, so no fixture could reach a minted value at all. `coordinator_epoch` is a per-coordinator 32-hex value minted per boot; the harness scrubs it by name to `<MINTED>` (#193), so the KEY is still asserted present while its per-run value is not compared.
